# parseJson

<link-summary>Parses JSON, and retries with a relaxed reader when strict parsing fails.</link-summary>

<web-summary>parseJson() — Parses JSON, and retries with a relaxed reader when strict parsing fails. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>json</code> · Since: 1.0.0 · <b>Deprecated</b></p>
</tldr>

> **Deprecated.** This function is deprecated and will be removed in future versions.

```typescript
function parseJson(value: string): object;
```

`JSON.parse` runs first. If it refuses, the text is tokenised again by rules that accept what hand-written configuration usually contains: unquoted keys and single-quoted strings.

Text that neither reader can make sense of throws. This is for configuration a person typed, not for a payload from a service — for that, `JSON.parse` and its error are clearer.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type     | Description                              |
| :-------- | :------- | :--------------------------------------- |
| `value`   | `string` | The text to parse. It must not be empty. |

## Returns

`object` — the parsed value.

## Throws

| Exception              | Condition                               |
| :--------------------- | :-------------------------------------- |
| `EmptyStringException` | the value is not a string, or is empty. |
| `SyntaxError`          | neither reader can parse the text.      |

## Examples

### Parsing

```javascript
parseJson('{"a":1,"b":[1,2]}'); // => {"a":1,"b":[1,2]}
parseJson("{a: 'x', b: 1}"); // => {"a":"x","b":1}
```
